hed: Oil settles Friday: Brent $104.61, WTI $100.05; week still up >8% as dual chokepoint persists
dek: Brent crude settled Friday at $104.61 a barrel and WTI at $100.05, according to Newsquawk and EnergyNow settlement prints — down on the day but still finishing a week with gains of more than 8% and both benchmarks above $100. U.S. diesel’s national average remained above $6 a gallon. Markets continued to price the dual chokepoint squeeze: Houthi advances near Bab el-Mandeb and constrained Hormuz flows from the U.S.–Iran tanker war.
alt: Oil refinery towers and industrial piping against a clear blue sky
caption: Refinery towers and process piping. File photograph used for layout; not from Friday’s oil settlement prints.
byline: Event summary from public market desks and named outlets

cl.body: Reuters, EnergyNow, and Newsquawk frame Friday’s settle — Brent $104.61 (−$3.02) and WTI $100.05 (−$2.43) — as a pullback from Thursday’s surge that still left both contracts above $100 for the week, with U.S. diesel’s national average above $6 a gallon keeping refined-product inflation in focus.

cr.body: EnergyNow’s weekly wrap and Reuters energy desks stress that despite Friday’s drop, Brent rose about 8.65% and WTI about 9.37% on the week as Houthi control near Mocha/Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz tanker risk kept dual-chokepoint premiums embedded heading into the weekend.

stack_blurb: Fri settle: Brent $104.61 / WTI $100.05; week >8%; diesel >$6.
